title: secp256k1-ecdlp: six-class rho with distinguished-point detection and unit-frame coefficients

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the six-class Pollard rho in proof.md (order-6 orbits under negation and the GLV endomorphism, Teske 16-adding walk, unit-frame coefficient registers updated by two residue adds per step, one-multiplication canonicalisation via beta^2 = -beta - 1, 4096 parallel walks, distinguished-point table keyed on canonical x with low 20 bits zero and 64-slot chain cap, addition budget equal to the least multiple of 4096 that is at least the 1/2-collision quantile t0, with no 5/4 length factor) recovers x with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^127.631096 total target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 with C=1000, including preprocessing, the incomplete-addition reserve, the distinguished-point store and solve reserve, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^115.943136 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^16.328837 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack: no quantum steps, no uncharged oracles, no amortisation across targets.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustive collision recovery on Z/n under the same order-6 multiplier action, 16-branch index, t0 birthday budget, unit-frame coefficient registers and distinguished-point detection used in proof.md. Sweeps budgets t0 and 2*t0. Checks the frame invariant alpha + secret*beta == canonical value on every step. Does not establish production instruction costs, hash-chain lengths, distinguished-point rate or secp256k1 field arithmetic.
